note: A constructed fixture, not a real county record. The place, the parties and the case numbers are
invented. What is copied from reality is the structure: the order of a minute, the way a staff
recommendation is recorded separately from the body's own vote, the fact that a tally can run in
either direction depending on how the motion was framed, and the fact that a continuance is not a
decision. Those are the things extraction gets wrong, so those are what a fixture has to contain.
Every quote below is verbatim from the document, which is what the regression suite verifies. If a
quote here stops matching, either the fixture changed or the normalisation did, and both should fail

_why_this_row_is_hard: The motion was to approve and it failed, so the outcome is a denial while the tally reads 2 to 4
in the direction of the motion. An extractor that records the tally without reading the verb
produces an approval on a 2 to 4 vote, which is the single most damaging error in the corpus.
Staff recommended approval and the body denied, so staff_recommendation and outcome disagree.
That disagreement is the signal, not a contradiction to be smoothed over.
Two case numbers, one decision. The relief is a rezoning and a special use permit together.

evidence.quote:
The motion failed on a vote of 2 to 4, with
Supervisor Nakamura absent.
The Planning Commission recommended denial by a vote of 5 to 2 on 20 August 2025.

_why_this_row_is_hard: A unanimous vote with no numbers. Section 6.4 forbids converting the word unanimous into a tally,
because the number of seats voting is not stated and a six seat board with one absence is not 6-0.

evidence.quote:
MOTION: Supervisor Ramirez moved to approve REZ-2025-0098. The motion carried
unanimously.

_why_this_row_is_hard: A continuance is not a decision. The outcome is continued, the row is censored, and decided_on is
null even though a vote was taken and carried 6 to 0. An extractor that reads carried as approved
turns a delay into an approval, and section 19.2 group B calls continuances the quiet killer of
timelines precisely because they look like progress.

evidence.quote:
The applicant has requested a further continuance to the
meeting of 9 November 2025.

_why_this_row_is_hard: A county initiated ordinance amendment, not an application. It belongs in the instrument schema
rather than the decision schema, and an extractor that files it as an application invents a
denial or approval for a project that does not exist.
The restrictions are numbers buried in prose: 2,000 feet, 55 dBA, 250,000 gallons per day. Pulling
them out as structured values is what makes setback_compliance_margin computable at all.
Adopted 5 to 1, which is the durability signal for the rule change hazard model.
expected_instruments.title: Data Centre Overlay District

evidence.quote:
establish a
Data Centre Overlay District, imposing a minimum setback of 2,000 feet from any
residentially zoned parcel

The motion
carried on a vote of 5 to 1, with Supervisor Nakamura absent.

The Arden Groundwater Alliance, represented by
counsel, submitted a petition bearing 1,240 signatures.

_why_this_matters: This is the sentence section 6.3 is about. The minute records that a motion failed; this records why,
and the why generalises to the next four decisions in the county. It is in the minutes here because
the fixture is a minute, but in practice it comes from the recording and is the reason transcription
expected_transcript_signal.quote:
Supervisor Alvarez stated that she could not support the application until the
county understood what it would do to the aquifer, and noted that she had been
asking the same question for six months.
expected_transcript_signal.attribution: a named supervisor, recorded as an aggregate objection ground and never as a prediction about her

must_not_extract.why: The Planning Commission's 5 to 2 recommendation is not a decision by the deciding body. Recording it as one would double count a single application and put a denial in the record on a date no denial occurred.
The petition signature count is not a speaker count and not a vote. It is a measure of organised opposition and belongs in the objection row.
Item 7 carried 6 to 0, but the motion was to continue. Reading the tally as an outcome converts a delay into an approval.
